store.summary: Ham radio tools: band check, RF math, greyline, propagation, satellite passes, POTA/SOTA, ID clock
store.description: From Ask Elmer, askelmer.com. Ham radio tools in your pocket. Band check: type a frequency and see the whole band as a bar with each license class's segments, whether you may transmit there, the power limit, how far you are from the edge, what's usually nearby (FT8, CW QRP, calling frequencies, 60 m channels) and quick antenna lengths. RF math: power, dB and S-units, SWR and return loss, Ohm's law, LC resonance and reactance, toroid winding for Amidon T and FT cores, and pi and T attenuator pads. Where & when: distance and beam heading to a grid or a call sign (with country and CQ/ITU zones), and sunrise, sunset and greyline at both ends. Propagation: solar flux, K and A and band conditions from hamqsl.com, plus an offline MUF estimate through the day. Satellites: the next passes of ISS, SO-50, AO-91, PO-101, RS-44, AO-7 and FO-29 with a sky plot and Doppler-corrected frequencies. POTA and SOTA: who's on the air now, parks and summits near you (kept for offline use) and an activation counter. A station clock in UTC with a 10-minute ID timer, and a searchable reference of Q signals, prosigns, CW abbreviations and RST. A USB GPS gives the time and your location, shared with the other Ask Elmer and Nomad apps; without one, type your grid. Fn+H shows help.
